title: Can I earn a reliable side-hustle selling custom ChatGPT prompts? My realistic experiment
excerpt: I tried turning prompt-engineering into a weekly side-hustle. Here’s what actually happened, the tools I used, and whether the model is sustainable for freelancers.
metaDescription: A freelancer’s hands-on test of selling custom ChatGPT prompts. Learn the workflow, earnings potential, pitfalls, and if the idea scales without burning out.
author: Ali Hamza
coverImageAlt: Person planning work with notebook and coffee
body:
## Why I doubted the "prompt hustle"

Everyone keeps talking about making money by selling AI prompts, but most stories sound like hype. I asked myself: can a freelancer actually turn a few minutes of prompt tweaking into a steady extra income without turning the job into a second full-time gig?

## The simple workflow I built

**Step 1 - Define a niche**
- I chose a narrow area I already understand: LinkedIn post ideas for tech founders. It kept research time low and demand felt real.

**Step 2 - Create a reusable prompt template**
- Using ChatGPT-4, I wrote a base prompt that asks for "three hook ideas, a short body, and a call-to-action". I saved the prompt in a Notion page for quick copy-paste.

**Step 3 - Set up a lightweight order form**
- I used Google Forms (free, no branding) to collect client details: niche, tone, length, and deadline. The form auto-emails me a summary.

**Step 4 - Automate the generation**
- With Zapier (free tier) I linked the form to a webhook that triggers a small Python script on Replit. The script injects the client’s inputs into the template and calls the OpenAI API.

**Step 5 - Deliver and invoice**
- The script returns the generated copy, which I copy into a pre-formatted Google Doc and share via a short-lived link. I invoice through PayPal with a flat $25 per prompt package.

## How much time did it actually take?

- **Initial setup**: about 4-5 hours spread over two evenings. Most of that was trial-and-error with the API call limits.
- **Per order**: 5-10 minutes to review the form, run the script, and polish the output. I kept a checklist to avoid missing client specifics.
- **Weekly overhead**: checking the inbox, tweaking the template based on feedback, and handling payments. Roughly 30-45 minutes total.

## Earnings reality check

During a four-week trial I received 12 orders, each at $25. That’s $300 gross, minus roughly $20 for OpenAI usage. Net profit landed around $260.

I didn’t hit the lofty numbers some hype posts claim, but the model proved it can cover a part-time freelance buffer without demanding a full schedule.

## What went right and what tripped me up

**What worked**
- **Niche focus** kept prompts relevant and reduced back-and-forth revisions.
- **Automation** removed the manual copy-paste step that usually eats time.
- **Flat pricing** avoided endless negotiations and kept the client experience smooth.

**What tripped me up**
- **Scope creep**: some clients asked for full blog outlines after the prompt was delivered. I had to set a clear boundary in the order form.
- **Quality variance**: ChatGPT can drift if the input isn’t precise. A quick read-through saved me from sending off-brand copy.
- **Visibility**: I relied on personal LinkedIn posts and a small Reddit thread. Without a dedicated landing page, traffic stayed low.

## Scaling thoughts - is it worth expanding?

If you’re comfortable with the OpenAI API and have a steady stream of niche clients, you can add a few upgrades:
- **Batch orders**: Offer a "10-prompt package" at a slight discount to lock in recurring revenue.
- **Template library**: Sell pre-made prompt packs for common use-cases (e.g., email subject lines, Instagram captions). This turns the service into a product.
- **White-label service**: Partner with a small agency that needs prompt content but lacks the technical setup.

Each upgrade adds complexity, so weigh the extra time against the marginal earnings. My rule of thumb: if a new feature adds more than 15 minutes per week, it probably isn’t worth it until you have at least double the order volume.

## Quick FAQ

**Q: Do I need a paid OpenAI plan?**
A: Not necessarily. The free trial gives enough tokens for a handful of prompts, and the pay-as-you-go pricing is cheap for short outputs. You can start with the free tier and upgrade only if volume grows.

**Q: Can I sell prompts without disclosing I use ChatGPT?**
A: Transparency builds trust. Most clients expect AI assistance and are fine with it as long as the final copy meets their standards.

**Q: How do I protect my prompt templates?**
A: Treat them like any other intellectual property - keep them in a private repo or password-protected Notion page. A basic terms-of-service note can deter misuse.

## Bottom line

Selling custom ChatGPT prompts can fill a modest side-hustle slot for freelancers who already juggle client work. The key is a tight niche, a repeatable automation pipeline, and clear boundaries on scope. Expect a few hundred dollars a month at the start; scaling to a larger income stream requires extra marketing and productization effort.

In my opinion, the biggest barrier is finding paying clients, not the technology. If you have an audience or can tap into a community that needs quick copy, the prompt service can become a reliable supplemental income.
